outcome: Every KPI item on an Activation Card names a measure; a 'quality' KPI with no scoring definition is refused naming the card and the item.
practical_value: One located defect and its class (critique run claude-seat-s12-btm-v4, unit u-016; the same shape on the Month 4, 5 and 10 cards): 'post quality, engagement quality' cannot be funded or governed.
stopping_condition: The real v1 pack refuses on the first unmeasured quality KPI; the same pack with the four quality items scored is accepted.
probe_goal: Whether KPI measurability is enforced by code.

approach_descriptions.hypothesis: A quality KPI must carry a scoring token or it is refused.
approach_descriptions.implementation: scripts/atom_check.py splits KPI items and checks quality items for a measure
approach_descriptions.predicted_tradeoff: the model must state scoring for quality KPIs

proof.success_criterion: v1 refused naming the card and item; scored items accepted.

phases.objective: Prepare the proof base, public identity and approval route before The Stop Line reaches the market through Signed by Humans.
Introduce The Stop Line publicly through Signed by Humans and direct owners, technical buyers, partners and talent to approved proof.
Keep The Stop Line visible between launch moments through proof, explanation, partner enablement and senior craft.
Use approved proof and third-party credibility to widen The Stop Line without widening the AI claim.

activation_cards.name: Public identity and proof-library lock
activation_cards.insight: The Stop Line cannot be credible if buyer-facing records conflict or AI claims are not tied to approved proof.
activation_cards.idea: Clean public identity and lock the proof library before any broad promotion of The Stop Line or Signed by Humans.
activation_cards.engagement_mechanic: The team reads public AI claims, identity records and proof labels in Month 1 against the approval route before anything is promoted.
activation_cards.desired_outcome: The B Team enters launch with fewer public contradictions and a proof base that can support The Stop Line.
activation_cards.targets: Public AI claims, buyer-facing public records and proof-library labels are read in Month 1 before launch assets proceed.
activation_cards.audience: Owners of midsize businesses, technical buyers, partners and senior Sofia talent.
activation_cards.message_pillar: The Stop Line makes AI easier to trust because it shows what is proved, who owns it and where the system stops.
activation_cards.kpi: Percentage of public AI claims linked to approved proof and unresolved public-profile conflicts closed.

activation_cards.name: The Stop Line proof page
activation_cards.insight: Buyers do not need a bigger AI promise; they need to see what is proved, who owns it and where the system stops.
activation_cards.idea: Create one owned page that introduces The Stop Line and shows each approved claim with proof type, senior owner and stated limit.
activation_cards.engagement_mechanic: Visitors inspect the proof behind the claim before they are asked to book a meeting or accept the AI story.
activation_cards.desired_outcome: The B Team has a public proof base that paid, earned, shared and sales activity can all point to.
activation_cards.targets: Approved claims, proof types, senior owners and stated limits are read in Month 2 before the proof page is cleared for launch.
activation_cards.audience: Owners of midsize businesses, technical buyers, referral partners and senior Sofia talent.
activation_cards.message_pillar: The B Team makes AI credible by showing The Stop Line before it promotes the AI claim.
activation_cards.kpi: Proof-page visits, time on page, qualified meeting clicks and percentage of public AI claims linked to approved proof.

activation_cards.name: Owner control message test
activation_cards.insight: Elena's preference for control and visibility is a strong hypothesis, but it is not settled buyer truth until owners compare the messages.
activation_cards.idea: Test a control-led message against an AI-capability message, both anchored in The Stop Line.
activation_cards.engagement_mechanic: Owners compare plain-language options that show visibility, ownership and early risk detection without asking them to become technical buyers.
activation_cards.desired_outcome: The B Team learns whether control should lead owner-facing communication before scaling the message.
activation_cards.targets: Owner reactions to control-led and AI-capability messages are read in Month 3 before the founder launch language is finalized.
activation_cards.audience: Owners of midsize businesses, led by Elena.
activation_cards.message_pillar: Owners get more control and visibility without having to become technical buyers themselves.
activation_cards.kpi: Preference split, comprehension score, trust lift, meeting intent and qualitative reasons for choice.

activation_cards.name: The Stop Line proof launch
activation_cards.insight: The Stop Line needs a public moment only after proof, ownership and limits are visible.
activation_cards.idea: Launch the proof page with approved press and owned materials that explain proof before promotion.
activation_cards.engagement_mechanic: Audiences are directed from launch coverage and owned channels to the proof page where claims can be inspected.
activation_cards.desired_outcome: The Stop Line becomes the named platform for The B Team's AI reputation story.
activation_cards.targets: Launch materials, proof-page readiness and approved AI claims are read in Month 4 before outreach begins.
activation_cards.audience: Owners of midsize businesses, technical buyers, partners and professional influencers.
activation_cards.message_pillar: The B Team makes AI credible by showing The Stop Line before it promotes the AI claim.
activation_cards.kpi: Proof-page visits, earned coverage quality, proof citations and qualified meeting clicks.

activation_cards.name: Signed by Humans founder launch post
activation_cards.insight: The human moment makes the AI story credible when a senior person visibly checks, owns and signs the work.
activation_cards.idea: Publish a founder-led launch post that explains Signed by Humans as the visible promise behind The Stop Line.
activation_cards.engagement_mechanic: Readers see the senior responsibility behind the claim and are directed to the owned proof page for evidence.
activation_cards.desired_outcome: Founder visibility increases while the public story stays inside the approved proof boundary.
activation_cards.targets: Founder copy, proof links and partner-share language are read in Month 5 before shared and paid amplification.
activation_cards.audience: Owners of midsize businesses, technical buyers, referral partners and senior Sofia talent.
activation_cards.message_pillar: Signed by Humans means senior people still own the outcome.
activation_cards.kpi: Founder-post reach, engagement quality, proof-page clicks, partner reshares and qualified inbound conversations.

activation_cards.name: Partner proof pack
activation_cards.insight: Referral partners can carry The Stop Line only if the approved proof is simple, repeatable and safe to share.
activation_cards.idea: Build a short partner pack that explains The Stop Line, Signed by Humans and the approved proof types behind each claim.
activation_cards.engagement_mechanic: Partners get language they can use without inventing claims or stretching evidence.
activation_cards.desired_outcome: Referral conversations become easier, more consistent and less exposed to unapproved AI claims.
activation_cards.targets: Partner language, proof types and approved reference material are read in Month 6 before partner briefings.
activation_cards.audience: Referral partners, ecosystem partners and enterprise buyers.
activation_cards.message_pillar: Every AI claim earns its place through approved proof before it reaches the market.
activation_cards.kpi: Partner pack downloads, partner briefings completed, referred qualified leads and claim-compliance checks.

activation_cards.name: Technical proof story
activation_cards.insight: Technical buyers need proof that AI supports delivery without taking ownership away from senior people.
activation_cards.idea: Publish technical artifacts and explanatory content that show the claim, the proof, the owner and the stop line.
activation_cards.engagement_mechanic: Technical buyers can inspect the artifact and use it in sales or architecture conversations.
activation_cards.desired_outcome: The Stop Line gains technical credibility without claiming autonomous AI.
activation_cards.targets: Technical artifacts, approval checks and proof labels are read in Month 7 before technical content is released.
activation_cards.audience: Technical buyers, chief technology officers and architecture owners.
activation_cards.message_pillar: AI supports the work, but senior people remain responsible for the claim, the delivery and the limit.
activation_cards.kpi: Technical artifact views, time on page, sales use and qualified technical conversations.

activation_cards.name: Senior craft story series
activation_cards.insight: Senior Sofia talent and careful buyers will believe the AI story only if it protects judgment rather than celebrating automation alone.
activation_cards.idea: Publish a recurring series under Signed by Humans that shows how senior people review work, make decisions and define the stop line.
activation_cards.engagement_mechanic: Readers see craft, judgment and responsibility inside AI-supported delivery.
activation_cards.desired_outcome: The talent story and buyer story reinforce each other without turning The B Team into a broad ethics platform.
activation_cards.targets: Craft stories, spokesperson materials and recruitment language are read in Month 8 before the series publishes.
activation_cards.audience: Senior Sofia talent and buyers who want craft behind AI-supported delivery.
activation_cards.message_pillar: Senior craft keeps judgment in the work.
activation_cards.kpi: Senior-talent engagement, profile visits, qualified candidate interest, buyer engagement and proof-page clicks.

activation_cards.name: Conversation Management and Observatory baseline
activation_cards.insight: A plan of bursts cannot hold reputation between moments; The Stop Line needs daily listening and disciplined response.
activation_cards.idea: Run the Conversation Management loop and Observatory newsroom with approved answers and escalation triggers.
activation_cards.engagement_mechanic: The team listens, triages, responds and escalates only within approved proof and stop-line limits.
activation_cards.desired_outcome: The Stop Line remains consistent in quiet months and under challenge.
activation_cards.targets: Questions, comments, AI-trust moments and approved answers are read in Month 9 and then daily before response.
activation_cards.audience: Owners, buyers, partners, employees, followers and professional influencers.
activation_cards.message_pillar: Proof comes before promotion.
activation_cards.kpi: Response time, issue resolution, message consistency, approved-answer reuse and escalation accuracy.

activation_cards.name: Earned validation outreach
activation_cards.insight: The credibility gap is not reach; it is whether independent voices can see proof worth citing.
activation_cards.idea: Pitch The Stop Line to journalists, analysts and named experts only after proof exists.
activation_cards.engagement_mechanic: Professional influencers receive a fact sheet, proof page and briefing route that keep the story inside approved evidence.
activation_cards.desired_outcome: Third-party validation makes The Stop Line harder to dismiss and gives paid, shared and owned channels stronger proof to carry.
activation_cards.targets: Earned pitch angles, proof citations and briefing materials are read in Month 10 before outreach.
activation_cards.audience: Professional influencers, journalists, analysts, named experts and enterprise buyers.
activation_cards.message_pillar: The B Team does not ask the market to accept an AI story without receipts.
activation_cards.kpi: Briefings secured, coverage quality, proof citations and qualified inbound conversations.

activation_cards.name: Employee advocacy push
activation_cards.insight: Employees and senior practitioners can make Signed by Humans visible when they repeat the story from lived craft, not slogans.
activation_cards.idea: Equip employees and advocates with approved social copy, craft examples and proof-page links.
activation_cards.engagement_mechanic: Employees share approved, role-specific posts that point back to proof and senior ownership.
activation_cards.desired_outcome: The Stop Line widens through credible employee advocacy without adding unapproved AI claims.
activation_cards.targets: Employee posts, craft examples and proof links are read in Month 11 before advocacy goes live.
activation_cards.audience: Employees, super fans, followers, senior Sofia talent and warm buyer audiences.
activation_cards.message_pillar: Senior craft keeps judgment in the work.
activation_cards.kpi: Employee participation, post quality, engagement quality, proof-page clicks and candidate interest.

activation_cards.name: Close scorecard and message recalibration
activation_cards.insight: The Stop Line remains durable only if measurement tightens the story instead of widening the claim.
activation_cards.idea: Close the executive scorecard, approve message changes and name next-year proof gaps.
activation_cards.engagement_mechanic: Leadership reads the year-end proof, trust, lead, partner and talent signals before approving the next cycle.
activation_cards.desired_outcome: The B Team knows what The Stop Line proved, what it did not prove and what must be built next.
activation_cards.targets: Scorecard results, message changes and proof gaps are read in Month 12 before the next-year plan is approved.
activation_cards.audience: Executive, partner, sales and communications owners.
activation_cards.message_pillar: The Stop Line holds the AI story inside approved proof, senior responsibility and visible limits.
activation_cards.kpi: Executive scorecard completion, message changes approved, next-year proof gaps named and claim-compliance rate.

pack.proof_building_order: Proof is built in the order the strategy can defend: first the cases and proof assets are cleaned, labelled and approved so The Stop Line has evidence to stand on; then thought leadership explains what the evidence means through Signed by Humans, founder posts, buyer explainers and senior craft stories; only after that does visibility widen through earned validation, partner activation, employee advocacy and paid amplification.

rollout.first_audience: The year speaks first to owners of midsize businesses, led by Elena, because the owner-control message must be tested before it becomes the lead public story.
rollout.then_widen: After owners understand The Stop Line and Signed by Humans, the story widens to technical buyers, referral partners, ecosystem partners, enterprise buyers, professional influencers, employees and senior Sofia talent, each receiving the same proof-first platform adapted to their role.

ownership.budget_frame: Internal content production unless paid amplification is approved.

pack.global_local: One core channel-agnostic toolkit travels across markets: The Stop Line platform, Signed by Humans signature, narrative, do-not-say lines, proof labels, approval route, message tracks, collateral templates and UTM format stay fixed, while local markets adapt hooks, spokespeople, language, local proof and market-specific tactics; global KPIs stay small and consistent, with local targets set from each market's baseline.
pack.markets_period: The campaign period is July 2026 through June 2027, ending no later than 30 June 2027, across the United States, the European Union and Sofia, Bulgaria.

pack.proof_building_order: Proof is built in the order the strategy can defend: first the cases and proof assets are cleaned, labelled and approved so The Stop Line has evidence to stand on; then thought leadership explains what the evidence means through Signed by Humans, founder posts, buyer explainers and senior craft stories; only after that does visibility widen through earned validation, partner activation, employee advocacy and paid amplification.

rollout.first_audience: The year speaks first to owners of midsize businesses, led by Elena, because the owner-control message must be tested before it becomes the lead public story.
rollout.then_widen: After owners understand The Stop Line and Signed by Humans, the story widens to technical buyers, referral partners, ecosystem partners, enterprise buyers, professional influencers, employees and senior Sofia talent, each receiving the same proof-first platform adapted to their role.

pack.global_local: One core channel-agnostic toolkit travels across markets: The Stop Line platform, Signed by Humans signature, narrative, do-not-say lines, proof labels, approval route, message tracks, collateral templates and UTM format stay fixed, while local markets adapt hooks, spokespeople, language, local proof and market-specific tactics; global KPIs stay small and consistent, with local targets set from each market's baseline.
pack.markets_period: The campaign period is July 2026 through June 2027, ending no later than 30 June 2027, across the United States, the European Union and Sofia, Bulgaria.
